general_harmonic_shift.name: general harmonic shift product-rule reduction
general_harmonic_shift.assumptions: A=sqrt(det(h))/N; B_ij=N*sqrt(det(h))*h^ij; Gamma^0=0 implies partial_t A=partial_j(A*beta^j)
general_harmonic_shift.scope: Coordinate components in a Cartesian periodic atlas; use connection differences for a global harmonic-map gauge on a general manifold.

global_solution_proof: The displayed face polynomials prove forward invariance of f,a,b,m,f_b>=0 and Ns>=Ns0.
The exact conserved total bounds every concentration and stored shell amount.
Ns>=Ns0>0 implies Ro-Ri>=Ro(Ns0)-Ri>0, so the vector field is smooth on a neighbourhood of the bounded invariant state set.
Local uniqueness and the ODE continuation theorem therefore give a unique solution for every finite future time; no state clipping or rollback is part of the equations.

shell_numerical_examples.scope: Numerical examples for the displayed well-mixed physical reactor ODE. Positivity/global existence follow from the separate analytic invariant-set proof. RK4 itself has no unconditional positivity assertion; no clipping was used.

continuum_theorem_scope.Einstein_scalar: Smooth periodic initial h>0,K symmetric,phi,Pi satisfying Hamiltonian/momentum constraints; N0>0 and smooth shift with harmonic initial gauge derivatives; smooth V (massless reference V=0). Harmonic reduction yields unique local gauge-fixed smooth development; geometric uniqueness is modulo diffeomorphism. The exact FLRW profile is defined for all T>=0.
continuum_theorem_scope.NSF_reference: Periodic ideal-gas Navier-Stokes-Fourier data in H^s, s>=6, positive initial density/temperature, positive constant shear viscosity/conductivity and lambda_v>=0. Local strong solution theorem; an arbitrary numerical flux or arbitrary coupled PDE does not inherit that theorem automatically.
continuum_theorem_scope.distinction: Exact identity checks establish the particular identities. The stated standard local PDE theorems and the supplied ODE continuation argument provide their respective existence scopes. No universal global regularity statement for all PDE couplings is claimed.
